answer.label: Written by
answer.sourceLine: These are genuinely Rosa Parks’s words, drawn from her faith memoir Quiet Strength (with Gregory J. Reed), where Wikiquote’s sourced section places them ↗. Note that the popular short form is a truncation: the full sentence continues — “knowing what must be done does away with fear.”

source.excerpt: I have learned over the years that when one’s mind is made up, this diminishes fear; knowing what must be done does away with fear.
trail: Wikiquote ↗ lists this in its sourced section under her memoir Quiet Strength (with Gregory J. Reed).
The full, unabridged sentence — “…knowing what must be done does away with fear” — is preserved on Goodreads ↗ and across quote archives.
A separate writer, Brendan Francis, is sometimes floated for the “fear” theme, but the specific wording here traces to Parks’s own book, not to him.
source.excerptNote: The line most people share stops at “…this diminishes fear” — but Parks’s sentence has a second half that completes the thought.
source.rightsHolder: The Estate of Rosa Parks and Gregory J. Reed; Zondervan (HarperCollins Christian Publishing)
source.rightsNote: This line comes from Quiet Strength, first published in the mid-1990s — well after 1931 — so it remains under copyright to Rosa Parks’s estate, co-author Gregory J. Reed, and the publisher, Zondervan. It is not in the public domain.

author.name: Rosa Parks
author.heading: About Rosa Parks
author.metaLine: 1913–2005 · American civil rights activist · "Mother of the Civil Rights Movement"
author.bio: Rosa Parks (1913–2005) was an American activist whose refusal to give up her bus seat in Montgomery, Alabama, on December 1, 1955, sparked the Montgomery Bus Boycott and became a catalyst of the civil rights movement. Late in life she reflected on faith, courage, and conviction in two memoirs — Rosa Parks: My Story (1992) and Quiet Strength (with Gregory J. Reed), the source of this line.

misattribution.heading: Genuine — but usually shortened
misattribution.intro: This one is authentically Rosa Parks. The issue is not who said it but how it’s quoted: the version that spreads online lops off the second half of her sentence.

items.why: Social posts and quote sites usually end at “…this diminishes fear,” dropping Parks’s completing clause — “knowing what must be done does away with fear” — which is present in the full sentence ↗.
Because Francis has his own oft-quoted lines about fear, his name sometimes surfaces near this theme, but the specific wording here belongs to Parks’s memoir, not to Francis.

misattribution.truthLine: The words are truly Rosa Parks’s, from her memoir Quiet Strength, as sourced on Wikiquote ↗ — just read the whole sentence, not the clipped half.

context.heading: Conviction over fear
lead: Rosa Parks spent decades framed by others as an accidental heroine — a tired seamstress who simply didn’t want to move. Her own writing pushes back on that myth. In Quiet Strength she casts her courage as a product of settled resolve: once the mind is decided, fear loses its grip.
detailsBody: The fuller sentence — “knowing what must be done does away with fear” — ties the thought to action, not just attitude, which is why the truncated meme version loses part of her meaning.
context.pull: When one’s mind is made up, this diminishes fear.
